name: Wisconsin
status_why: No statewide count on the night: the Commission publishes only the canvass, and its site and the largest counties' sites show scripts a challenge.
system: No statewide election-night reporting: the Wisconsin Elections Commission publishes only canvassed results (county-by-county workbooks) weeks later; 72 county clerks post their own unofficial results (PDF summaries, some vendor ENR sites).

races_in_feed: On Nov 3, 2026: statewide (Governor and the other constitutional offices), Congress, Legislature, and only three county offices (sheriff, clerk of circuit court, coroner) per CLAUDE.md. City and school offices are elected in April.
local: Yes, entirely: Milwaukee County (county.milwaukee.gov, Cloudflare), Dane (elections.danecounty.gov, Cloudflare captcha), Waukesha, Brown, Racine (not checked).
how_counted: County clerks post unofficial results on the night; the state publishes results only after its canvass.
count_order: Not split in a form a program can read.
vote_types: Unknown live. Milwaukee's central count of absentee ballots reports late and in large batches (well known; not checked here); county summaries do not split it out in a machine-readable way.

scout_plan: Wisconsin has no official live feed a script can read: the state publishes nothing until the canvass, and the big counties sit behind Cloudflare. Election Night should show Wisconsin as 'official count arrives with the canvass' and, on the night, either (a) John saves the Milwaukee and Dane summary PDFs by hand a few times (both are PDF reports, so a reader per county), or (b) the page links out to each county clerk's results page without numbers. Final results come from the WEC canvass workbook (Browser-pane carry-out, as the kit already does). Local races on Nov 3 are only three county offices, so the county PDFs cover them.
